senses.definition: A clear, deep, red variety of corundum, valued as a precious stone.

quotes.text: They respond instantly to the faintest rustling in the covert of a sheaf of Ulysses S. Grants, or the homely, rustic tinkle of a wheelbarrow full of rubies being jounced along over a nightclub floor.

Although there are dozens of different types of gems, among the best known and most important are diamond, ruby and sapphire, emerald and other gem forms of the mineral beryl, chrysoberyl, tanzanite, tsavorite, topaz and jade.
quotes.reference: 2012 March 25, Lee A. Groat, “Gemstones”, in American Scientist, volume 100, number 2, archived from the original on 14 Jun 2012, page 128:

quotes.text: When now I thinke you can behold such sights, / And keepe the naturall Rubie of your Cheekes, / When mine is blanch'd with feare.
quotes.reference: c. 1606 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Macbeth”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene iv]:

quotes.text: Elgin. Topaz a Saltier and Chief Ruby, on a Canton Pearl a Lyon Rampant Saphyr, which last is their paternal Coat; and the Field Topaz, and Saltier, and Chief Ruby, was the Arms of King Robert the Bruce, they altering the Field from Pearl (as he bore it) to Topaz.
quotes.reference: 1720, Francis Nichols, Rudiments of Honour, page 296:

quotes.text: The Field is Ruby, on a Bend Topaz, three Martlets Diamond. [...] Checkie Topaz and Saphire, a Fesse within a Bordure Ruby, by the Name of Clifford.
quotes.reference: 1726, John Guillim, The Banner Display'd; Or, an Abridgment of Guillim, page 504:

quotes.text: (1) Pearl, a Cross, Ruby, with the Effigies of our Saviour thereon, Topaz, born in Memory of one of the Family's fighting against the Turks. (2) Topaz, a Chief Indented, Saphire. (3) Ruby, three covered Cups, Topaz [...]
quotes.reference: 1754, John Lodge, The Peerage of Ireland; Or, a Genealogical History of the ..., page 71:

senses.definition: A ruby hummer, a South American hummingbird, Clytolaema rubricauda.
(uncountable, printing, UK, dated) The size of type between pearl and nonpareil, standardized as 5½-point.
(typography) A pronunciation guide written above or beside Chinese characters.
Of a deep, red color; ruby-red.
(transitive, poetic) To make red; to redden.

quotes.text: With sanguine drops the walls are rubied
